question.problem: Margaret is studying and analyzing a culture of bacteria. From a certain moment, she notices that the number of bacteria $B(t)$ in the culture grows according to the formula $B(t)=500\cdot {2}^{t},$ where $t$ denotes the time in hours. How many bacteria will there be after $4$ hours?

current_example.problem:
The formula $M(t)=128 \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{4} \right)^{t}$ gives the mass (in grams) of a radioactive calcium isotope after $t$ years.
What mass of isotope remains after $3$ years?
current_example.worked_solution:
To get the mass of the isotope after $3$ years, we evaluate the function at $t=3.$ Substituting $t=3$ into the function $M(t)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =128{(\frac{1}{4})}^{t} \\  & =128{(\frac{1}{4})}^{3} \\  & =128\cdot \frac{{1}^{3}}{{4}^{3}} \\  & =128\cdot \frac{1}{64} \\  & =\frac{128}{64} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $3$ years, there will be $2$ grams of isotope remaining.
